title: How to Make Meta Muse Apply to Jobs for You: 2026 Connector Guide
summary: Meta Muse can browse the web and fill forms, but Meta names no job-application connector. A 2026 guide to Muse connectors for job search, résumés and…
body_markdown:
**No. Meta names no Muse connector that applies to jobs for you, and Tsenta has no documented Muse setup yet.** What you can use today is Muse’s own browser. Meta says it can fill out online forms, so it can work through an application on a company’s career site under the approval settings you choose. Meta Muse is Meta’s personal AI agent. It is not The Muse, the job board at themuse.com.


Because Muse is an agent that can browse and act on websites, it can open tsenta.com and work in your Tsenta account in its browser, the way you would. That is ordinary browsing, not a Muse connector or integration.


This guide covers the Muse connectors Meta documents, what Muse can do on its own, how to have it apply to one role with you in control, and where Tsenta’s MCP server could fit.


Checked November 20, 2026. Tsenta publishes this guide and sells one of the services in it. We read Meta’s Muse help center, its newsroom posts, muse.ai, the Muse Supplemental Terms and Meta’s connector platform docs, plus each third-party page we mention. We did not run a signed-in Muse application test. Meta says the full connector list lives inside the app, so your list may show more than Meta’s public pages do.


## Meta Muse or The Muse? Which one this guide means


Search results mix the two, and so do some AI answers.


**Meta Muse** is the agent Meta[launched on September 8, 2026](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/) . Meta calls it “a personal AI agent” that “doesn’t just answer questions, it actually does the work.” It works in Muse Secure VM, which[muse.ai](https://muse.ai/) calls “a persistent, isolated Linux computer with a full browser.” You reach it in the Muse app on iOS and Android, at muse.ai, in WhatsApp and in a[Mac app](https://www.meta.com/blog/meta-connect-2026-everything-we-announced/) . Meta’s Muse Spark model powers it.


**The Muse** , at[themuse.com](https://www.themuse.com/) , is a separate job board and career advice site with company profiles. It is not Meta’s agent, and nothing below is about it.


Meta’s newsroom lists Muse in the US, Canada, Singapore and, since November 17, 2026,[Australia](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/11/muse-is-now-available-in-australia/) . You must be 18 or older, and Meta’s[subscription help](https://www.meta.com/help/subscriptions/1021145227643680/) says Muse is “in limited testing” and not available in all locations yet.


## Can a Muse connector apply to jobs for you?


Not one you can install from Meta’s public list. Here is every route we found and what each does today.


Route Applies for you? What it does in a job search


**Muse’s own browser** It can fill out and submit web forms, with the approvals your settings require Opens career sites, fills application forms, lets you watch or take over ([Meta’s browser help](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/2124746764949121/) )


**Connectors Meta names** No Email, calendar, files and work apps. None for job boards or applicant tracking systems


**A custom connector Muse creates** Only if the service offers a way to apply, and Meta does not review it Muse can build one for a service not in its list ([Meta’s connectors help](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/1687253048996149/) )


**FindYourCareer** (third party) No, by its own FAQ Searches and reads job listings in Muse


**Job Search Crew** (third party) No, you apply Finds roles, drafts applications and logs them in your Google Sheet


**Tsenta’s MCP server** No documented Muse setup yet In Claude, ChatGPT (Business, Enterprise and Edu for applying), Cursor and Codex: finds roles, tailors your résumé and submits on supported company career sites


So no connector Meta names applies to jobs for you today, but Muse itself can fill out an application, one form at a time, under Meta’s approval rules. A connector would apply through a service built for it. Muse’s browser works the way you would, page by page, and stops when your settings or Meta’s safety checks say it should.


## Muse connectors Meta documents, and which help a job search


Meta’s[connectors help](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/1687253048996149/) says you connect from **Settings** , then **Connectors** : tap **Connect** next to a connector, read the details and tap **Continue** . You can also just ask, for example “Connect my Gmail.” Many connectors can be limited to reading data without taking actions.


Meta does not publish one full list. Its small business post says you can[see the full list of connectors in your Muse app settings](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-small-business) , “with more to come.” These are the connectors Meta names in public, sorted by what they do for a job hunt.


Connector, as Meta names it Use in a job search Where Meta names it


**Gmail** Read job alert emails, application confirmations and recruiter replies[Canada](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/11/meta-welcomes-loblaw-as-first-canadian-retail-partner-to-muse/) ,[Singapore](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/10/muse-is-now-available-in-singapore-the-worlds-first-personal-ai-agent-built-for-everyone/) and Australia posts


**Google Calendar** Interview times and prep reminders Canada, Singapore and Australia posts


**Notion** Résumé versions, a job tracker database, interview notes[Small business post](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-small-business) and[Connect 2026 recap](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/the-biggest-news-from-connect-2026/)


**Dropbox and Box** Résumé files, transcripts and portfolios Small business post


**Canva, Figma and GitHub** Portfolio work for design and engineering roles Small business post and Connect recap


**Granola and Zoom** Notes from calls Small business post


Meta also names Slack and Asana, which matter less for a search. It names no connector for Google Drive, Google Docs, LinkedIn, Indeed, any other job board or any applicant tracking system on the pages we read.


### Gmail, Notion and Google Drive: which are official?


Gmail and Notion are official: Meta names both, along with Google Calendar. Google Drive is not named on any Meta page we read, so treat a third-party list that includes it as unconfirmed until you see it in your own **Settings** , then **Connectors** .


### Custom connectors and connectors Meta reviews


For a service not in the list, Meta’s connectors help says “you can ask Muse to create a Custom Connector,” which “can involve retrieving API information from the service.” Meta “doesn’t review custom connectors or how they use your information, so grant access with caution.” Its[security post](https://muse.ai/blog/security-and-safety-for-ai-agents-our-approach-with-muse) adds that Muse can write them for services “if they have their own APIs or CLIs.” None of the user-facing Meta pages we read describes adding a remote MCP server by its address.


Companies can also submit a connector for Meta’s review through the[Muse Connector Platform](https://platform.muse.ai/docs) . There, a sensitive write, such as a purchase or sending an email, asks on every use and “cannot be set to Always allow.”


## What Muse can do for a job search on its own


No Meta page we read mentions résumés, cover letters or job applications. The one job-related line is in Meta’s[voice launch post](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/11/introducing-muse-ai-voice-expressive-avatars/) : “Prepare for a job interview, run through a presentation, or talk through a pitch.” Everything else below is a general Muse feature applied to a job search.


- **Find and research roles.** Muse’s built-in[skills](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/2797651547267109/) include browsing the web, compiling research and drafting documents. It can read a posting, pull out the requirements and compare them with your background. Meta names no job-search feature.
- **Draft a tailored résumé and cover letter.** Meta’s[getting started guide](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/1331373868832401/) says Muse can “read, summarize, edit, or generate artifacts including PDFs, spreadsheets, documents.” Upload your résumé and a job post and ask for a version for that role. Meta also says Muse “may be inaccurate,” so read every line before it goes anywhere.
- **Fill out applications.** Meta’s[browser help](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/2124746764949121/) lists “Filling out online forms” among browser tasks. You can tap **Open browser** to watch, **Take control of the browser** to pause Muse, or **Stop the task** . Passwords go to the Secure Credentials Store, out of the model’s view.
- **Track and follow up.** Muse can[run recurring tasks](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/1484325780075655/) daily, weekly or on a custom interval, such as a Monday check of your inbox. It can also build a[Space](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/11/introducing-spaces-customize-muse-app/) , a custom view you describe that keeps itself up to date from connected apps. Meta’s examples include an order tracker, so a job tracker is a fair ask.
- **Email.** Muse can have its own email address, per Meta’s[Connect 2026 recap](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/the-biggest-news-from-connect-2026/) . Meta’s connectors help says Muse will not take many important actions, like sending an email, without your approval by default.
- **Practice interviews.** Voice mode lets you rehearse answers out loud. Meta says voice is available only in some countries.


## Rules and limits before Muse applies for you


**Approvals.** Under **Settings** , then **Permissions** , Meta’s[approval help](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/1385290430137537/) sets two choices for connectors and two for web access. For connectors, **Ask for some actions** asks before every write action and important read actions, and **Always ask** asks before any action. For web access, **Ask for some actions** asks “when your information may be shared or it visits a website that is unfamiliar,” and **Always ask** asks “before accessing any website.” Depending on the action, a request can offer Allow once, Allow for this task, Allow for this site, Always allow or Deny. Meta’s[design post](https://muse.ai/blog/how-we-designed-muse) says the default “allows for standard browsing of the web and stops for anything hard to undo.”


**Safety checks.** Meta’s security post says browser classifiers watch for “Attempted submission of high risk forms” and “either block the action or prompt the user to review what is about to happen.” Meta does not say whether a job application counts as a high-risk form, so expect some prompts you did not plan for.


**Terms.** The[Muse Supplemental Terms](https://muse.ai/terms) , effective November 17, 2026, say you “will maintain meaningful human oversight over all actions taken” and should not make state-changing actions “without appropriate human review and approval prior to execution or granting pre-authorization.” They forbid circumventing any third party’s terms of service, “including but not limited to circumventing any paywalls or CAPTCHAs,” and concealing that Muse is not human where the law requires disclosure. You are “solely responsible for the actions Muse takes.” If you want employers to know an agent helped, Meta’s help says you can ask Muse to add a note that content was generated by your AI agent.


**Cost.** Muse is free with a weekly usage limit that refreshes. As of November 20, 2026, Meta’s[subscription help](https://www.meta.com/help/subscriptions/1021145227643680/) lists Muse’s Power plan at $20 a month with 500M Muse tokens a week. Muse’s Maximum plan is $100 a month with 3B Muse tokens a week. Meta publishes no number for the free allowance.


## How to have Muse apply to one job, step by step


These steps use features Meta documents. We have not run them end to end in a signed-in account.


1. **Give Muse your master résumé.** Upload it in chat, or connect Notion, Dropbox or Box where you keep it.
2. **Tighten approvals while you learn.** In **Settings** , then **Permissions** , set web access to **Always ask** so Muse checks with you before it opens any site.
3. **Pick one role on the employer’s own career site.** Paste the link and ask Muse to list the requirements and what your résumé is missing.
4. **Ask for a tailored PDF.** Read every line against your real experience, fix what is wrong and keep the version you approve.
5. **Ask Muse to fill the form and stop before the final submit.** Tap **Open browser** to watch. Take control for CAPTCHAs, verification codes, salary questions and essay answers, which are yours to give.
6. **Submit only after you check the filled form.** Choose **Allow once** rather than a standing permission until you trust the pattern.
7. **Log it.** Ask Muse to add the role to a Notion database or a tracker Space, and set a weekly recurring task to check Gmail for replies.


Sid Saladi’s[Substack post](https://sidsaladi.substack.com/p/make-meta-muse-apply-for-your-jobs) describes a fuller version with a setup prompt, a morning task and batches the author approves. It reports one day in which the setup “found 17 roles, submitted 12 on company career sites, hit 1 company’s own application limit and parked 4.” That is one person’s run, and most of the walkthrough is paywalled. It also relies on a résumé skill made for Claude, while Meta’s help says Muse skills “are developed by Meta and are already part of Muse.”


## Tsenta as a Meta Muse connector: not documented yet


Tsenta’s MCP server connects your own AI assistant to your Tsenta account. Meta says Muse can write its own custom connectors for other services, but its public Muse pages do not describe adding a remote MCP server by its address. If your Muse account supports custom remote MCP servers, give it Tsenta’s server address and sign in with OAuth. Tsenta has no Meta Muse guide, so check the tools Muse lists after you connect.


The server address is` https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp` . In the assistants Tsenta documents, sign-in opens in your browser, where you sign in to Tsenta and approve access, and the assistant never sees your password.


### What Tsenta does through the assistants it documents


Tsenta publishes step-by-step setup for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Codex at[tsenta.com/mcp](https://tsenta.com/mcp) . Connected there, your assistant can:


- **Find roles.** Get roles ranked against your profile, filtered by location, remote work, pay and date posted. Tsenta watches 300,000+ company career pages.
- **Tailor your résumé.** Per role, in Honest mode, which rewords your experience, or Aggressive mode, which rewrites more freely and may stretch claims, with a cover letter when the form takes one.
- **Submit applications.** One role, a batch or a job link you paste, submitted in the cloud on supported company career sites.
- **Track.** Read the status of every application Tsenta starts, move roles through Applied, Interviewing, Offer, Rejected or Ghosted in your tracker (including roles you applied to elsewhere), and read recruiter emails in your Tsenta inbox.


An application request queues work. It does not mean the employer has received it yet. With résumé auto-approval off, each tailored résumé waits for your approval, and form review stops before the final submit on employer systems that support pausing. One approval gives the assistant every available Tsenta tool on your account, including tools that edit your profile and reply to emails, and whether it asks before each action depends on the assistant, not on Tsenta.


### If your Muse account can add it


If Muse does connect, these are the asks Tsenta suggests for it:


- “Find part-time marketing jobs near Seattle that fit my profile.”
- “Apply to the best one with a tailored résumé and a cover letter if the form takes one.”
- “Did any recruiter reply to my applications this week?”


Connecting costs nothing extra. Your first 25 applications are free with no card. USD global pricing is Starter at $19 a month for 600 applications, Pro at $39 for 1,500 and Power at $99 for 4,500 per 30-day cycle; see[pricing](https://tsenta.com/pricing) for your market. On Starter and Pro you choose each role and Tsenta submits it. Auto Apply, which submits eligible roles within your filters without per-role approval, needs Tsenta’s Power plan.


### Tsenta as a Claude connector or ChatGPT app today


If you want applications submitted from a chat now, use an assistant Tsenta documents. In Claude Desktop or claude.ai, open **Customize** , then **Connectors** , choose **Add custom connector** and paste the server address. Custom connectors work on every Claude plan, and Free allows one, per[Anthropic’s help center](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp) . See[Tsenta for Claude](https://tsenta.com/connectors/claude) . In ChatGPT, add Tsenta as a custom MCP server, which OpenAI now calls a plugin. Applying needs full MCP support, which[OpenAI lists](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-connecting-custom-mcp-servers-in-chatgpt) on ChatGPT Business, Enterprise and Edu on the web. Our[help article](https://help.tsenta.com/connect-claude-chatgpt-mcp) and[connection guide](https://tsenta.com/blog/connect-ai-job-search-agent-to-claude-chatgpt-2026) walk through both, and our[best Claude connectors](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-claude-connectors-job-search-2026) and[best ChatGPT apps](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-chatgpt-apps-job-search-2026) guides compare other options.


### Where Muse wins, and where Tsenta wins


Muse wins on breadth and price to start. It is free with a weekly usage limit, it works by voice, and its browser can try any website, including career sites Tsenta cannot submit on. It also handles email, calendar and errands in the same chat.


Tsenta wins when you want applications sent without driving a browser. It finds roles from the career pages it watches, and it tailors and submits on supported company career sites. Each application it sends lands in your tracker, and recruiter replies land in your Tsenta inbox, whether you use the dashboard or an assistant. Tsenta also works in iMessage and WhatsApp.


## Other Muse job-search setups


### FindYourCareer: search and read jobs in Muse


[FindYourCareer’s Muse guide](https://findyourcareer.io/blog/how-to-find-jobs-with-meta-muse-ai) says its connection lets Muse search and read jobs, and its FAQ answers whether Muse will apply through it with “No… You choose which vacancies to open and apply for yourself.” It needs an eligible FindYourCareer Career Pass, which it says includes 3,500 unique jobs a month. It tells you to give Muse’s Custom Connectors a server address and notes that “Setup may vary by account.” Where it wins: it is the only job-search connection for Muse we found with published setup steps.


### Job Search Crew: drafts in Muse, you apply


[Job Search Crew](https://jobsearchcrew.com/) sets up what it calls a crew inside Muse or Grok Bot, and says it brings you roles “within hours of posting, your application already drafted.” Your roles, contacts and notes land in a Google Sheet and Drive you own, and it says “Review, apply, and get in early,” so applying stays with you. As of November 20, 2026, it lists the first month free, then $19.99 a month, and needs a Google account. Our[Grok Bot plugins guide](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-grok-bot-plugins-job-search-2026) covers it from the Grok Bot side.


## Which route to choose


- **You want a few careful applications and will watch each one:** Muse’s browser, with **Always ask** on and the steps above.
- **You want Muse to find roles and keep the list:** Gmail for alerts, plus a Notion tracker or a Space. FindYourCareer adds a job search connection if you have a Career Pass.
- **You want applications submitted and tracked without driving a browser:** Tsenta through Claude, Cursor, Codex or ChatGPT Business, Enterprise or Edu today, or the Tsenta dashboard. LoopCV also says it submits applications from[Claude](https://www.loopcv.pro/apply-with-claude/) and[ChatGPT](https://www.loopcv.pro/apply-with-chatgpt/) , and is free to start, but its pages do not mention Muse. Our[Tsenta vs LoopCV comparison](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-loopcv) covers caps and pricing.
- **You are still picking an assistant:** read[Meta Muse vs Grok Bot vs Instinct](https://tsenta.com/blog/meta-muse-vs-grok-bot-vs-instinct-job-search) ,[Instinct connectors for job search](https://tsenta.com/blog/instinct-ai-connectors-job-search-2026) ,[how AI agents apply to jobs](https://tsenta.com/blog/how-ai-agents-apply-to-jobs-2026) ,[résumé-tailoring connectors by assistant](https://tsenta.com/blog/ai-assistant-connectors-tailor-resume-2026) and[tracking applications with AI assistants](https://tsenta.com/blog/track-job-applications-ai-assistants-2026) . For servers beyond Muse, see the[best MCP servers for job search](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-mcp-servers-job-search-2026) .


## Frequently asked questions


### Is there a Muse connector that applies to jobs for me?


Not as a documented setup yet, because Tsenta has no Meta Muse guide and Meta’s public Muse pages do not describe adding a remote MCP server by its address. Meta’s public Muse pages also name no connector for job search or job applications. Muse’s own browser can fill out online forms, so it can work through an application on a company’s career site under the approval settings you choose. If your Muse account supports custom remote MCP servers, give it Tsenta’s server address and sign in with OAuth.


### What are the best Muse connectors for job search?


The most useful Muse connectors for a job search are the ones Meta names for email, calendar and files. Use Gmail for job alerts and recruiter replies, Google Calendar for interviews, and Notion, Dropbox or Box for your résumé and tracker. Meta names no connector for job boards or applicant tracking systems. Third-party setups exist too: FindYourCareer says its Muse connection searches and reads jobs, and Job Search Crew drafts applications for you to send.


### Can a Muse connector auto apply to jobs?


No connector that Meta names auto-applies to jobs. Muse can submit forms in its own browser, but Meta’s terms say you must keep meaningful human oversight and review state-changing actions before they happen or pre-authorize them. Muse’s approval settings decide when it stops to ask you. In Tsenta, Auto Apply, which submits eligible roles within your filters without per-role approval, is an account setting that needs Tsenta’s Power plan.


### Is there a Meta Muse LinkedIn connector for job search?


No LinkedIn connector appears on Meta’s public Muse pages, and neither does Indeed or another job board. Meta says the full connector list is in Muse’s settings, so check there. You can still connect Gmail, let your LinkedIn job alert emails arrive there, and ask Muse to find each role on the employer’s own career site.


### Are Meta Muse connectors for Google Drive, Notion and Gmail official?


Gmail and Notion are official Muse connectors that Meta names on its own pages, and so is Google Calendar. Google Drive is not named on any Meta page we read on November 20, 2026. If a service is not in your connector list, Meta says you can ask Muse to create a custom connector, which Meta does not review.


### Is Meta Muse the same as The Muse job board?


No. Meta Muse is Meta’s personal AI agent, launched on September 8, 2026, which you use in the Muse app, at muse.ai or in WhatsApp. The Muse, at themuse.com, is a separate job board and career advice site. This guide is about Meta’s agent.


### Can I connect Tsenta to Meta Muse?


Not as a documented setup yet. Meta says Muse can write its own custom connectors for other services, but its public Muse pages do not describe adding a remote MCP server by its address. If your Muse account supports custom remote MCP servers, give it Tsenta’s server address and sign in with OAuth. Tsenta publishes step-by-step setup for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Codex.


### How much does Meta Muse cost?


Meta says Muse is free with a weekly usage limit that refreshes. As of November 20, 2026, Muse’s Power plan costs $20 a month for 500M Muse tokens a week and Muse’s Maximum plan costs $100 a month for 3B. Meta says Muse and its subscriptions are in limited testing and not available in all locations, and you must be 18 or older.
